problem: Section 1 says the ESB "sits between providers and consumers", but the figure places the Messaging layer (ESB, queue) below the Services layer, next to Data. A student reading both will be unsure whether the bus fronts the services or backs them.
fix: Either move Messaging above Services in the stack, or change the note to something like 'queues, events used by providers' and keep the ESB description as sitting between consumer and provider.

problem: PUT is described only as "replaces", and Q5 asks only which verb replaces a resource. Standard HTTP also lets PUT create a resource at a URI chosen by the client if none exists there, so the replace-only wording can mislead.
fix: Say 'PUT creates or replaces the resource at a known URI (it replaces the full representation)', and in Q5's answer add that PUT can also create the resource when it is absent.

problem: The text points to other material as plain words: "See Chapter 2.2 for the HTTP basics" and "see Unit 3, Virtualization and Containers". On a phone these are not tappable and the chapter id is not given.
fix: Use the chapter link form, for example "See Chapter 2.2 for the HTTP basics" and a link to the virtualization chapter id for Unit 3.
